Rebuild time spread is 0.5–1%. A candidate whose population mean is ~0.752 passes seeds 0–2 only ~40% of the time. Re-keeping a fast candidate therefore needs a population mean of ≥0.7545, or else repeated single-build attempts, which the gate forbids.

2. Hidden per-step fixed cost, and my misses on E046, E050 and E056.
   - Elementwise and optimizer traffic is priced too low by everyone, me included.
   - Each step launches three separately compiled Muon graphs (fp32 buffer, bf16 Newton-Schulz on every filter) plus fused SGD. Their cost does not depend on resolution, so they weigh most in the 20/24 px phases.
   - Freezing removes a whole Muon call. That is why the freezes beat their FLOP share.
   - The unproposed levers:
     - one batched NS graph across groups;
     - skipping the NS/update for frozen-LR groups during the anneal tail, when the LR is near 0;
     - updating group 3 less often at 20 px.
   - I also suspect autotune choices differ by build. E050's 5.206 vs my 5.33 and E056's 4.95 suggest wall time moves by about 1% with kernel selection. Time comparisons below 1% need CUDA-event timing.

3. Muon renormalizes filters and fixes the update norm. A filter's ||ΔW||/||W|| therefore tracks its LR schedule, which makes I094's filter curves tautological. Freeze cost is roughly linear in the LR integral removed while downstream layers are still adapting, not a threshold:
   - E037: −0.4 pp
   - E055: −0.15 pp
   - E053: ~−0.2 pp

4. Steps carry accuracy; early pixels do not. E026 and E033 were free. Step cuts traded near the dial's rate (~1–1.5 s/pp). E054, E051 and E053 cut per-step work on layers that were still learning, and lost.

5. The whitening bias runs at 64× LR. Detaching it at 6% fixes it to 20 px antialiased statistics, so I expect a small loss (~0.05–0.1 pp) for a ~0.3–0.5% saving. That is roughly a wash at the dial's rate.

6. Settled by reading the code:
   - BN scale is already frozen (requires_grad=False), so I092 is a no-op.
   - Only fine labels are supplied (TrainingData has images and labels only), so H1.8 is blocked.
   - Filter wd is inert because the filters are renormalized.

7. The end-game is at a local optimum: averaging, LS schedule, LR floor and BN recalibration all hurt or did nothing (E025, E030, E032, E044).

8. Best paths:
   - (a) Fuse the NS/Muon updates into one graph and skip updates for near-zero-LR groups. This is identical math, so it gives time at no accuracy cost.
   - (b) ReLU (E056: −4.7% time for about −0.15 pp), plus a top-up of ~0.25 epoch.
   - (c) Stack E046-style cuts only after a booster lifts the population mean.

9. On the PCIe judge, expect times 5–10% higher.

   - Freezing removes a whole Muon call. That is why the freezes beat their FLOP share.
   - The unproposed levers:
     - one batched NS graph across groups;

   - I also suspect autotune choices differ by build. E050's 5.206 vs my 5.33 and E056's 4.95 suggest wall time moves by about 1% with kernel selection. Time comparisons below 1% need CUDA-event timing.

3. Muon renormalizes filters and fixes the update norm. A filter's ||ΔW||/||W|| therefore tracks its LR schedule, which makes I094's filter curves tautological. Freeze cost is roughly linear in the LR integral removed while downstream layers are still adapting, not a threshold:
   - E037: −0.4 pp

   - E053: ~−0.2 pp

4. Steps carry accuracy; early pixels do not. E026 and E033 were free. Step cuts traded near the dial's rate (~1–1.5 s/pp). E054, E051 and E053 cut per-step work on layers that were still learning, and lost.

5. The whitening bias runs at 64× LR. Detaching it at 6% fixes it to 20 px antialiased statistics, so I expect a small loss (~0.05–0.1 pp) for a ~0.3–0.5% saving. That is roughly a wash at the dial's rate.

forecasts.reason: E046 rebuilt. The dial difference of ~0.1 pp is at the size of the noise even with 20 seeds plus σ_build, so a 0.6–2 s/pp range is hard to exclude.
TrainingData supplies only fine labels, so the idea is blocked by its own step 0. Any measurement would be the tip rerun.
BatchNorm.__init__ already sets weight.requires_grad=False, so the check closes by code read and nothing changes.
Saves ~0.3–0.5%, below the rebuild spread. Freezing the 64×-LR bias on 20 px statistics probably costs ~0.05–0.1 pp, which straddles the 0.05 pp threshold.
Muon's fixed-norm filters make ||ΔW||/||W|| follow the LR schedule. The curves cannot separate E028 (free) from E037 (costly) without restating the schedules.

cruxes: What share of a 20/24 px step is fixed cost: the three Muon/NS graphs plus SGD, Lookahead and launches? If it is ≥15%, fusing NS into one graph and skipping updates for groups whose LR is near zero is an identical-math time win that no one has queued.

Does E057's three-build data show a correlated shift in the 20-seed mean (σ_build ≥0.08 pp)? This decides whether near-feasible candidates (E052, E046) can ever be re-kept, given the single-build seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 check.
What is the ReLU swap's population cost on fresh seeds? If it is ≤0.1 pp, then ReLU plus a +0.25 epoch top-up dominates E049 by ~3%.
